A4.2 Data Preprocessing HL

Topic A4: Machine Learning | Cleaning & Shaping the Data

Retrieval Practice

Recall A4.1 (fundamentals) before going HL.

  1. What is the difference between training and inference?
  2. What’s the difference between regression and classification?
  3. Why are GPUs useful for ML?

Press Down for answers

Answer 1

What is the difference between training and inference?

Training: learning/updating model weights using data. Inference: using a trained model to predict on new data.

Answer 2

What’s the difference between regression and classification?

Regression: predicts a number. Classification: chooses a category.

Answer 3

Why are GPUs useful for ML?

They can perform many calculations in parallel (useful for matrix operations).

The Big Question HL

🤔 Why do ML projects spend so long on data…

instead of “just choosing an algorithm”?

❌ Common misconception: “The algorithm will handle messy data.”

Bad inputs often produce bad predictions — confidently.

✅ Reality: HL preprocessing improves accuracy, efficiency, and fairness.

Garbage in → garbage out.

HL Data cleaning

What problems in raw data can distort a model?

Missing values (null/blank fields)

Duplicates (over-representing some records)

Incorrect data (impossible dates, negative ages)

Outliers (extreme values that may be errors or rare cases)

Common strategies

Remove bad records (when justified).

Impute missing values (mean/median, or model-based).

Cap/transform outliers (depends on context).

🧠 Quick Check HL

A dataset for predicting exam grades contains:

- missing attendance values

- duplicate student records

- an outlier score of 999

Outline two cleaning steps you would take.

Remove or merge duplicates to avoid bias from over-represented records.

Handle missing values (impute or remove) and investigate the outlier (999) to correct/remove it.

HL Feature selection

Why might fewer input variables produce a better model?

Removes irrelevant/noisy inputs → reduces overfitting risk.

Speeds up training and improves interpretability.

Two common approaches

Filter: choose features using statistics (e.g., correlation).

Wrapper/embedded: choose features based on model performance.

HL Dimensionality reduction

What if your data has hundreds of features?

Reduces model complexity and training time.

Can improve generalization by removing noise.

Helps visualization by reducing data to 2D/3D.

Key distinction

Feature selection: keeps some original features.

Dimensionality reduction: creates new, fewer features (e.g., PCA components).

🧠 Quick Check HL

You have 500 features from sensors in a smart building.

Explain one reason to use feature selection and one reason to use dimensionality reduction.

Feature selection: remove irrelevant sensors to reduce noise/overfitting and speed training.

Dimensionality reduction: compress many correlated sensor readings into fewer components.

Misconception Check HL

True or False: “Dimensionality reduction always improves accuracy.”

False. Reducing dimensions can remove useful signal if done poorly.

The goal is to balance simplicity with keeping information that matters for prediction.

Key Takeaways HL

  • HL Data cleaning fixes missing values, duplicates, incorrect data and outliers.
  • HL Feature selection keeps useful variables and reduces noise/overfitting.
  • HL Dimensionality reduction compresses features to simplify models and speed training.
  • Preprocessing often has a major impact on performance and fairness.
